pages.title: What you will learn
pages.body:
> 🔤 **Strand 2 — Algebra**
Using letters and symbols to describe patterns, relationships and unknown quantities.

> 🎯 **Content standard** (B9.2.1)
- B9.2.1.1 — Demonstrate the ability to construct tables of values for pairs of linear relations, graph the relations in a number plane and determine the intersection of the lines to solve simultaneous linear equations.

> 🎯 **In this chapter you will learn to:**
- construct tables of values for two linear relations and draw their graphs on the same axes
- read missing values of ordered pairs from the graphs
- solve two linear equations simultaneously by finding the point of intersection of their graphs

pages.body:

pages.title: Tables of values and graphs of two relations
pages.body:
> 🎯 **You will learn to:** Construct a table of values for two linear relations and graph the relations.
Curriculum indicator B9.2.1.1.1
## ✏️ Example 5.1
Copy and complete the table of values for y₁ = −x + 5 and y₂ = x − 3 for x from −3 to 3, and draw both graphs on the same axes.
**Solution**
| **x** | **−3** | **−2** | **−1** | **0** | **1** | **2** | **3** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| y₁ = −x + 5 | 8 | 7 | 6 | 5 | 4 | 3 | 2 |
| y₂ = x − 3 | −6 | −5 | −4 | −3 | −2 | −1 | 0 |
[[fig:m9-f07]]
Figure 5.1: y = −x + 5 and y = x − 3
The lines cross at **(4, 1)**, just outside the table's range — extend the lines to see it. Check: −4 + 5 = 1 and 4 − 3 = 1 ✓.
## ✏️ Example 5.2
Complete the tables of values for x − 2y = −2 and x − 2y = 2 for x from −2 to 2, and draw the graphs.
**Solution**
Make y the subject: x − 2y = −2 ⟹ y = [[x + 2/2]]; x − 2y = 2 ⟹ y = [[x − 2/2]].
| **x** | **−2** | **−1** | **0** | **1** | **2** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| y = (x + 2) ÷ 2 | 0 | 0.5 | 1 | 1.5 | 2 |
| y = (x − 2) ÷ 2 | −2 | −1.5 | −1 | −0.5 | 0 |
[[fig:m9-f08]]
Figure 5.2: x − 2y = −2 and x − 2y = 2 are parallel
Both lines have gradient [[1/2]], so they are **parallel** and never meet. The pair of equations has **no solution**.

pages.title: Reading missing values from graphs
pages.body:
> 🎯 **You will learn to:** Use graphs of two linear relations to determine subsequent missing elements in ordered pairs of the relations.
Curriculum indicator B9.2.1.1.2
## ✏️ Example 5.3
The graph shows y = −x + 4 and y = x − 2.
[[fig:m9-f09]]
Figure 5.3: y = −x + 4 and y = x − 2
a) Find the coordinates of the point of intersection. b) Find the values of y on both lines when x = −1. c) Use the graph to complete the table.
| **x** | **−3** | **−2** | **−1** | **0** | **1** | **2** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| y = −x + 4 |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| y = x − 2 |  |  |  |  |  |  |
**Solution**
a) The lines cross at **(3, 1)**.
b) When x = −1: y = −(−1) + 4 = **5** on the first line and y = −1 − 2 = **−3** on the second.
c)
| **x** | **−3** | **−2** | **−1** | **0** | **1** | **2** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| y = −x + 4 | 7 | 6 | 5 | 4 | 3 | 2 |
| y = x − 2 | −5 | −4 | −3 | −2 | −1 | 0 |
> ✏️ **Practice:** Exercise 5.2, at the end of section 5.3, covers this section too. Tap **Quick check** to try its questions.

pages.title: Solving simultaneous equations graphically
pages.body:
> 🎯 **You will learn to:** Use graphs to solve equations involving two linear relations.
Curriculum indicator B9.2.1.1.3
> 🔑 **Key idea: Simultaneous equations** — Two equations in the same two unknowns form a pair of **simultaneous equations**. Their solution is the pair (x, y) that satisfies **both**. Graphically, it is the **point of intersection** of the two lines.
## ✏️ Example 5.4
Solve graphically: y = −x + 7 and y = 2x + 1.
**Solution**
| **x** | **0** | **1** | **2** | **3** | **4** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| y = −x + 7 | 7 | 6 | 5 | 4 | 3 |
| y = 2x + 1 | 1 | 3 | 5 | 7 | 9 |
[[fig:m9-f10]]
Figure 5.4: The lines meet at (2, 5)
The lines intersect at (2, 5), so **x = 2, y = 5**. Check: −2 + 7 = 5 ✓ and 2(2) + 1 = 5 ✓.
## ✏️ Example 5.5
From the graph, find the values of x and y that make both y = x + 4 and y = 6 − x true.
**Solution**
[[fig:m9-f11]]
Figure 5.5: y = x + 4 and y = 6 − x
The lines meet at (1, 5): **x = 1, y = 5**. Check: 1 + 4 = 5 ✓; 6 − 1 = 5 ✓.
> 🎯 **BECE tip** Choose at least **three** x-values for each line (two to draw it and one to check). Use a sharp pencil and a suitable scale — an inaccurate graph gives an inaccurate solution. Always check your answer in both equations.

pages.title: Chapter 5 summary
pages.body:
- Make a table of values for each relation, plot both lines on the same axes.
- The point of intersection gives the solution of the simultaneous equations.
- Parallel lines (equal gradients, different intercepts) never meet: no solution.
